city.record_kind: the official long-term record NOAA keeps for the city, joining several sites over the years
city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 45°F was the 17th coolest November 13 high (tied) of 135 since 1876, the coolest since 2022.
text.p_yest: The high of 45°F was the 17th coolest November 13 high (tied) of 135 since 1876, the coolest since 2022. The normal high for the date is 59°F, and the record is 75°F (1938, 1958, 1964). The low of 35°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Asheville has nearly stopped setting record lows
text.p_rec: If Asheville's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Asheville has set 19 standing record lows, far fewer than the 72 that chance alone would give, and 69 record highs, close to the 72 that chance alone would give. The 1930s hold the most record highs of any decade (48). Asheville's all-time high is 100°F, on August 21, 1983.
text.t_chg: Asheville has warmed, days and nights alike
text.p_chg: Across 131 complete years: Asheville's average low has risen +0.10°F per decade (95% range +0.04 to +0.17), about +1.4°F since 1889. Asheville's average high has risen +0.16°F per decade (95% range +0.10 to +0.22), about +2.2°F since 1889.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 6 of 12 months. Highs rose in 8 of 12 months.
text.p_rain: Asheville's yearly precipitation has risen +0.99 inches per decade (95% range +0.64 to +1.35), about +15.2 inches since 1872. The 1991–2020 normal is 49.6 inches a year. The wettest year was 2018 (79.48 in); the driest, 1925 (22.79 in).
